tasks.heading: Engineering walkthrough — Hand-computed rank fusion and a false evidence match
tasks.title: V06/C05 — Hybrid retrieval and reranking
tasks.content:
## Engineering walkthrough — Hand-computed rank fusion and a false evidence match

**Original synthetic example:** lexical search ranks documents A, B, C; semantic search ranks C, D, A. Using Reciprocal Rank Fusion with illustrative `k=60`, the score for A is `1/61 + 1/63 ≈ 0.03227`; for C it is `1/63 + 1/61 ≈ 0.03227`; B and D each contribute one list hit. A and C tie under these assumptions, **without any claim that either is factually correct**. Different handling of missing ranks, duplicate IDs or list truncation changes the result.

A restricted document can be top-ranked in one retriever: fusion must not reveal its title or score through results, explanations or related links. Reranking may improve relevance for permitted candidate texts but cannot repair a source-revision mismatch or transform a speculative claim into published evidence. The [Elasticsearch RRF reference](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/elasticsearch/rest-apis/reciprocal-rank-fusion) defines the general rank-only fusion mechanism; actual feature/version requirements must be pinned for production.

| Stage | Necessary gate | Failure consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Retrieve lexical/vector candidates | Source snapshot and permission scope | Authorized evidence omitted or forbidden text leaked |
| Fuse ranks | Stable identity and declared missing-rank behavior | Duplicate content treated as independent corroboration |
| Rerank | Preserve source boundaries and disclose heuristic nature | Plausible but stale claim promoted over current authority |
| Answer | Verify material claims against original source/version | Confident answer when evidence is insufficient |

**Proposed experiment, not run:** hand-verify small fusion scores, then evaluate real held-out questions with authorized judgment sets and deliberately contradictory/stale snippets. If relevant sources remain absent, **refuse a substantive architectural conclusion and request evidence** instead of increasing model confidence or traversal depth.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->

tasks.heading: Three original workload decisions
tasks.title: Multiple writers and offline conflicts
tasks.content:
## Three original workload decisions

| State | Candidate merge | What remains outside the guarantee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per-device diagnostic contribution count | Merge each stable device component by maximum, then sum | Deduplicating a real-world action performed on two devices |
| Set of descriptive labels | Track unique add tags; remove only observed tags | A concurrent unseen add can remain present |
| Limited set of approved seats | Authoritative reservation or preallocated rights | Unrestricted offline approvals cannot preserve the global limit |

For the counter, device P advances its component from 3 to 4 and device Q from 5 to 7. Merging components gives 4 + 7 = 11 regardless of duplicate state delivery. Reusing a retired device identifier or decrementing its component breaks this construction. A device reset therefore needs a new identity and an explicit retention policy. This is an arithmetic illustration, not a production measurement.

For labels, replica P removes the add tags for “draft” that it has seen. Replica Q concurrently adds “draft” using a fresh tag. Their merge retains Q's addition under an observed-remove design. That is deterministic, but a user expecting removal to override every concurrent addition will find it incorrect. Choose the product meaning first.

For seats, imagine a limit of two and one existing approval. P and Q each approve a different person while disconnected. Each local state appears valid; the combined state contains three. Taking the union converges and still violates the capacity invariant. Last-writer selection can conceal one approval after the fact, but cannot undo an external action already performed on it.

tasks.heading: Engineering walkthrough — Provision, shed, optimize or simplify under uncertain prices
tasks.title: Capacity planning and cost/performance trade-offs
tasks.content:
## Engineering walkthrough — Provision, shed, optimize or simplify under uncertain prices

**Original synthetic envelope:** a hypothetical catalogue expects 100–400 requests/s depending on a publication event, with 10% writes and one hot resource. Direct unit prices and exact staffing rates are **unknown**. The architect must compare not a single monthly VM bill but correct peak outcomes, shared database budget, retention, multi-zone idle capacity and time to recover from overload.

| Candidate | Potential strength | Variable that may reverse choice |
|---|---|---|
| Provision extra replicas | Faster response to burst if app CPU is bottleneck | Shared DB lock/pool remains the limit; unused warm capacity costs money |
| Shed/defer optional work | Protect invariant and critical journeys | Product cannot accept deferred confirmation or unfair priority |
| Optimize query/key access | Less demand per correct operation | No meaningful backend query cost in measured bottleneck |
| Simplify/remove unnecessary distributed hop | Lower operational and retry overhead | True isolation/deployment requirement outweighs coordination cost |

A defensible cost model exposes quantities: instance-hours, data bytes×retention, egress GB, high-cardinality time-series, human on-call hours, migration person-days, repeated backup/DR exercises and expected rework risk. It must vary each cost input over a documented plausible range rather than pretend an invented provider price is a source-backed rate.

**Synthetic sensitivity rule:** if one candidate only wins when app instance prices fall 90% or when a known critical correctness constraint is waived, mark it fragile or inadmissible. Report correct throughput per total operating cost *conditional on* tested workload, not raw RPS per VM. **Proposed experiment, not run:** test steady/peak/degraded load, keep shared-state integrity, record actual unit use and capacity drain after overload; select an option only after gating security and recoverability separately. The existing Well-Architected cost guidance supports modeling categories, not numerical market forecasts.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->

tasks.heading: 1. Two unsafe dual-write orders
tasks.title: Outbox publication and ordering
tasks.content:
## 1. Two unsafe dual-write orders

Consider an original invented device-reservation system: it records an accepted reservation and notifies another component. Naive sequence **DB then broker** can commit the reservation and crash before publishing. Naive sequence **broker then DB** can publish a purported acceptance and later roll back the reservation.

[Richardson's Transactional Outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox) records publication intent together with the business state in a **single local** transaction, then uses a relay. It explicitly notes that a relay may send a message more than once.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C["Command with effect ID"] --> TX["Atomic local DB transaction"]
    TX --> S[("Reservation authority state")]
    TX --> O[("Outbox event intent")]
    O --> R["Relay / CDC"]
    R --> B["Broker with possible redelivery"]
    B --> I["Consumer inbox / effect guard"]
    I --> D[("Consumer-owned durable effect")]
```

**Text alternative:** one local transaction commits both reservation truth and a publication-intent record. A relay sends from that record. Downstream consumers must handle duplicates and record their effects under their own transactional authority. There is **no atomic transaction spanning all illustrated components**.

### Publication truth table

| Failure point | What can be durable | Recovery requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Before local commit | Neither business state nor outbox intent | Retry command with stable business identity |
| After local commit, before relay | Business state and outbox intent | Relay resumes from durable source |
| Broker receives event, relay loses acknowledgment | Broker may store event; relay still sees unsent | Duplicate publication must be tolerated |
| Consumer commits, then loses broker acknowledgment | Consumer-owned effect may already exist | Inbox or effect identity prevents duplicate state |
| Consumer must call another external system | Local DB cannot atomically cover that call | External effect identity or reconciliation |
| Event arrives after newer entity state | Stale event may be replayed | Defined version/order conflict and quarantine |

The source's event-intent guarantee is conditional on **actual atomic insertion**. Writing a so-called outbox record after a completed business transaction still leaves a failure window.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->

tasks.heading: Engineering walkthrough — Reconnect cannot recover unpersisted stream items
tasks.title: Asynchronous APIs and streaming: demand, deadlines and cancellation
tasks.content:
## Engineering walkthrough — Reconnect cannot recover unpersisted stream items

**Synthetic scenario:** a device-status server streams numbered updates over gRPC to a remote consumer. The network drops after the server sends sequence 41 but before the consumer can acknowledge it; the server emits 42 while the client is offline. Transport flow-control windows influence buffered bytes **while connected** but do not constitute a durable event log or replay cursor.

| Contract decision | Option A: transient live feed | Option B: resumable durable subscription |
|---|---|---|
| Owner of buffered state | Process/session with bounded bytes | Named storage/log with retention and sequence identity |
| Disconnect after sending 41 | Missing/duplicate 41 may be acceptable, explicitly labeled | Client resumes from last *durably processed* sequence; dedup and replay required |
| Slow consumer | Backpressure, drop/coalesce or explicit disconnect | Lag budget, quotas and replay horizon must be declared |
| Publisher restart | Session resumes from current state only | Rebuild cursor from durable authority; cannot replay what was never persisted |

If updates mean *current temperature*, dropping interim samples may be an acceptable product policy. If updates mean *irrevocable financial postings*, an ephemeral stream is not sufficient. Cancellation of a receive loop does not roll back a posting that another system already committed. This trade-off is separate from choosing gRPC vs WebSocket vs SSE.

**Proposed protocol (not implemented):** include `stream_id`, monotonically interpreted position within a declared partition, schema version, snapshot ID and retention boundary. Client checkpoints a position only after its required local effect is durable. Inject disconnect before/after acknowledgment, server restart, slow consumer and position expiry; return an explicit "resnapshot required" response when replay is impossible. The chapter's gRPC flow-control and Reactive Streams sources support bounded transport/demand semantics, not a durable replay guarantee.

<!-- /tycho-question-source -->
